Content Type: Live dynamic system (AJAX/form-driven; academic year -> semester -> type -> unit -> group cascade)
RAG Chunking Strategy: Not chunked / not embedded. Excluded from static RAG corpus - resolve via live query (API call or headless-browser scrape) triggered by the agent's "timetable lookup" tool, keyed on Academic Year, Semester, Type and Unit/Group parameters.
Update Frequency / Recrawl Cadence: Real-time (query on demand, no caching beyond session)
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: No stable canonical page per course; content is rendered client-side after user selections, so a crawler/RAG indexer will only see empty selectors. Requires a dedicated connector/tool rather than a document ID in the vector store.

RAG Chunking Strategy: Semantic section-based chunking by H2/H3 heading (e.g. per degree class, per requirement type), ~300-500 tokens/chunk, each chunk tagged with its parent heading as metadata for citation.
Update Frequency / Recrawl Cadence: Low - review annually or on Senate/Academic Registrar policy change
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: Cross-references Grading and Examinations pages; consider adding a related_doc_id link for retrieval-time context stitching.

Content Type: Static policy page with embedded tables (marks-to-grade scale; CGPA classification scale) and FAQ-style Q&A blocks
RAG Chunking Strategy: Hybrid chunking: (1) table-aware chunking - keep the Marks/Letter Grade/Grade Point table and the CGPA classification table each as one atomic chunk with a text preamble restating column headers; (2) Q&A-pair chunking for the 'What can I do if...' / 'How do I appeal?' sections, one Q&A per chunk.
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: High-value document for the RAG agent - grading scale table must not be split mid-row or numeric lookups will fail.

RAG Chunking Strategy: Section-based chunking by heading, with any procedural/appeal steps preserved as ordered-list atomic chunks so step sequence is not broken.
Update Frequency / Recrawl Cadence: Medium - review each semester before exam period
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: Likely overlaps with Grading (appeals) - dedupe or cross-link during ingestion to avoid contradictory retrieved chunks.

RAG Chunking Strategy: Section-based chunking by heading (eligibility criteria, exam structure, application steps), ~300-400 tokens/chunk.
Update Frequency / Recrawl Cadence: Low-Medium - annually, ahead of the admissions cycle
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: Eligibility criteria are high-stakes for user decisions - flag chunks containing dates/deadlines for freshness checks.

RAG Chunking Strategy: Record-level chunking - one chunk per listed institute (name + brief description + link), rather than splitting by token count, so a single-entity query retrieves one complete record.
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: Pair with MAK-KB-007 and MAK-KB-008 under a shared academic_structure tag for routing/disambiguation queries (institute vs college vs department).

RAG Chunking Strategy: Record-level chunking - one chunk per college, with nested department names kept together in the same chunk as their parent college.
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: Central reference for routing student inquiries to the correct College/Department support ticket queue.

Content Type: Static overview/index page linking to sub-directories
RAG Chunking Strategy: Hierarchical chunking - one chunk per academic-unit category (Colleges, Institutes, Centers, Affiliated Institutions) preserving the parent/child relationship as metadata.
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: Largely a navigational hub; low standalone answer value but useful for disambiguating which unit handles a given query.

RAG Chunking Strategy: Section-based chunking by heading (platforms, access instructions, support contacts).
Update Frequency / Recrawl Cadence: Medium - review each semester as tools/links change
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: Verify the MUELE portal link stays current at each recrawl; broken links here degrade user trust quickly.

Content Type: Directory / listing page (links out to courses.mak.ac.ug catalogue of 140+ programmes)
RAG Chunking Strategy: Record-level chunking per programme/college grouping for the listing page itself; treat the linked courses.mak.ac.ug catalogue as a separate, larger sub-corpus requiring its own paginated ingestion job.
Update Frequency / Recrawl Cadence: Medium-High - review each admissions cycle / whenever new programmes are added
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: Highest-volume document family - budget a separate crawl/ingestion pipeline for courses.mak.ac.ug rather than treating it as one page.

RAG Chunking Strategy: Section-based chunking by scholarship scheme/heading, each scheme (eligibility, funder, deadline) kept as one atomic chunk.
Update Frequency / Recrawl Cadence: High - scholarship listings open/close each term
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: Time-sensitive content - strongly recommend a valid_until or last_verified field per chunk to prevent the agent citing expired scholarships.

Content Type: Static policy page, likely with fee-schedule tables
RAG Chunking Strategy: Table-aware chunking - one atomic chunk per fee-schedule table (programme/college level), plus section-based chunking for payment procedure text.
Update Frequency / Recrawl Cadence: High - review annually at fee-structure announcement
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: Numeric fee data is a common support-ticket trigger if stale; prioritize in the re-crawl schedule and consider a human-in-the-loop verification step before re-indexing.

RAG Chunking Strategy: Section-based chunking with ordered-step (numbered) chunks preserved intact for procedural sequences (e.g. registration steps, add/drop deadlines).
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: Frequently asked in student support tickets - good candidate for a short FAQ-style summary chunk in addition to the full procedure chunks.

RAG Chunking Strategy: Step-preserving chunking - one chunk per numbered instruction step, with an introductory chunk summarizing prerequisites (documents, portal link, fees).
Notes / Ingestion Caveats: Pair with the Application Portal URL (apply.mak.ac.ug) referenced in-page; verify that link resolves at each recrawl.
